long_biography.plain_text:
Philip Green made deal-making and close operational control the centre of a four-decade career in British retail. He began by buying surplus and distressed clothing stock, judging its resale value and turning around chains before progressing to larger acquisitions. The purchase and break-up of Sears strengthened his reputation for extracting value from established retail brands.

Green bought BHS in 2000 and acquired Arcadia two years later through the Green family's Taveta vehicle. At Arcadia, he became known for inspecting stores and intervening directly in merchandising. The model brought its greatest prominence through fashion brands, but its durability proved limited. BHS collapsed after Green sold it, and Arcadia entered administration in 2020 before its best-known brands passed to new owners.
